### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/service-knowledge`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **33** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-knowledge/package.json`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/vitest.config.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-knowledge/package.json`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/index.ts`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/vitest.config.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f1b56daa855c9b1cfd07e9ad91856dd8b4370058` — the merge of head `502329806381bd19b8afeb5717b9c8df3a3fa918` into base `57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f1b56daa855c9b1cfd07e9ad91856dd8b4370058 && git checkout f1b56daa855c9b1cfd07e9ad91856dd8b4370058
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b 502329806381bd19b8afeb5717b9c8df3a3fa918 && git checkout -B drift-repro 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b && git merge --no-ff 502329806381bd19b8afeb5717b9c8df3a3fa918

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 57445a699810a0545d8b3a7649a77327d47fb18b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Read at 2026-11-24T13:02Z. First record on this head. The implementer is the project thread on branch `claude/project-thread-wuyeiy`; this review ran in an isolated sub-agent of the same session, from the card, the PR, the diff and the check-runs only. An earlier record on the superseded PR #34223 (comment 6907077911, head `ba9ec457`) was read as history; every judgment below was re-derived on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, default boot (no `KnowledgeServicePlugin`): narrowed, and named right.** `builtinSettingsManifests` is 9 (no `knowledge`); `aiSettingsManifest` carries no `embedder_*` key, no `embedder` group and no `test_embedder` button; the default `actionHandlers` map registers neither `knowledge.test` nor `ai.test_embedder`. At the door (`settings-routes.ts`): `GET` / `PUT /api/settings/knowledge` and `POST /api/settings/knowledge/test` answer `404 UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE`; a `PUT` of an `ai.embedder_*` key answers `400 UNKNOWN_KEY`; `POST /api/settings/ai/test_embedder` answers `400 SETTINGS_ACTION_FAILED` through `runAction`'s no-handler branch. These are the answers the PR body and the changeset name.
- **Accept-set, service mounted: unchanged.** `contributeKnowledgeSettings` registers the same `knowledgeSettingsManifest`, the same six embedder specifiers and button (moved verbatim into `aiEmbedderSettingsSpecifiers`) and the same two handlers. `registerManifest` keeps the previous `actions` map when it replaces a namespace, so `ai.test` survives the join; write predicates and option sources live in separate maps and survive too; the env-override report is de-duplicated, so the second registration of `ai` does not repeat it.
- **Registration order: right.** `optionalDependencies` names the literal `com.objectstack.service.settings`, which equals `SETTINGS_PLUGIN_ID`. `SettingsServicePlugin.init()` registers its manifests, handlers and the `settings` service, so the `ai` page exists when the knowledge plugin's `init()` reads it. `service-settings` does not depend on `service-knowledge`, so the new package dependency adds no cycle (`Validate Package Dependencies`: success).
- **Public surface.** `@objectstack/service-settings`: six symbols added to the package entry (`knowledgeSettingsManifest`, `knowledgeTestActionHandler`, `aiSettingsManifest`, `aiEmbedderSettingsSpecifiers`, `withAiEmbedderSection`, `aiTestEmbedderActionHandler`); `builtinSettingsManifests` and `aiSettingsManifest` shrink. `@objectstack/service-knowledge`: `contributeKnowledgeSettings`, `knowledgeSetupNavItem`, `KNOWLEDGE_SETUP_NAV_BUNDLE_ID` and one type added; a hard dependency on `@objectstack/service-settings`. `@objectstack/platform-objects`: `SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS` loses `nav_settings_knowledge` (29 to 28). All stated in the changeset.
- **Setup entry.** The contributed bundle has the shape of the branding precedent in `settings-service-plugin.ts` (`namespace: 'sys'`, `navigationContributions` into `group_configuration`), is registered after the `knowledge` manifest and only when a settings service took it, and keeps `requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']`. Its position moves from between AI and Data Lifecycle to after the static Configuration entries (priority 110).
- **Stored rows: no read widening.** `namespaceReadScope` reads a row of an unregistered namespace at the default capability, so I checked whether stored `knowledge.*` rows open to a `setup.access` holder once the namespace is unregistered. They do not: the manifest is `scope: 'global'`, its rows live in `sys_platform_setting` and `sys_platform_setting_audit`, and both objects gate on `manage_platform_settings` at the object. `ai.embedder_*` rows stay under the registered `ai` namespace.
- **In-repository readers of the narrowed keys: none at runtime.** `embedder_*`, `test_embedder` and the `knowledge` namespace are read only by the manifests, `cloud-managed-settings.ts` (hide list), translations and tests. `content/docs/**`, `apps/docs/**` and `skills/**` name none of them.
- **Hosted readers (cloud `16b444e`).** `service-ai` `applyEmbedder` reads `getNamespace('ai')`, which answers declared keys only; with no `embedder_provider` it builds nothing and does not throw. Its `registerAction('ai', 'test_embedder', …)` runs from a `kernel:ready` hook, so it cannot throw (`ai` stays registered) and, where the knowledge service is mounted, it still replaces the form-check handler the knowledge plugin registered at `init()`. No hosted runtime mounts `KnowledgeServicePlugin`. `controlPlaneSettingsManifests` passes `ai` through unchanged and names `knowledge` only in a comment. The PR body's account of the hosted runtime holds.
- **Pins.** The default-absent pin judges by status and `error.code`, each case with a control. The contribution suite compares a mounted kernel with a bare one built by the same function, with the knowledge plugin `use`d before the settings plugin. The two corpus pins and `cloud-managed-settings.pin.test.ts` re-join the moved declarations explicitly, so they measure what they measured before. The CLI pin moves 37 to 36 with an explicit `not.toContain('nav_settings_knowledge')`. The checklist restates 9 builtins, 10 served namespaces and 46 Setup destinations.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the true arm and reads the same on the PR body and the changeset. The `!` title, the **BREAKING** paragraph and a "What to do" paragraph are present.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is true: no schema key, accepted value or metadata type moves; a settings manifest is a runtime registration. So `patch` is the level, on exactly the three packages the diff moves (`service-settings`, `service-knowledge`, `platform-objects`). `packages/cli` changes a test only.
- ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` fits: no export is retired, and stored rows are not rewritten.
- `Skills-docs: none` is true (see ①).
- The changeset's migration paragraph is incomplete on stored credentials: S2 below.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Check-runs on this head, read at 13:02Z: 66 runs — 21 success, 9 skipped, 35 in progress, 1 failure.** The gate verdicts are not in. Green so far include `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Validate Package Dependencies`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Type Check · source gates` and `Type Check · debt ledger`. Every `Test Core` and `Test UI` shard, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Build Core` and five `Lint` families were still running. This PASS is a judgment of the contract and the tree; it is **not** a reading that CI is green. The seat reads convergence.
- **The one red is stale, and must be re-run.** `PR-body guards` failed at 12:54:13Z on the duplicate-claim step: #33933 was still claimed by draft PR #34223, which was closed at 12:55:06Z. Its other three steps passed. The check re-runs on `edited` / `synchronize`; it has not re-run yet.
- **Escalated: the dogfood battery is owed on this head, and the PR checks will not supply it.** The PR body says the battery "runs on this PR's GitHub checks". It does not: `ci.yml`'s `dogfood` job is conditioned on `github.event_name != 'pull_request'`, the three shards read `skipped` on this head, and the bare `Dogfood Regression Gate` context reads `success` over legs that never ran. The only battery reading the PR carries is at `1b210ee4f6`, before two merges of `main` (the second brought #33891's hosted projection onto the same files). The rule for a `(narrowing)` PR is one full battery on the final head, checked before queue entry (`os-dev.md` definition of done; L1 checklist). The seat owes that run, or a ruling that the queue run stands in for it, and the body sentence should say which.
- **Escalated: two cloud tests pin the retired default and go red at the next framework pin move.** `packages/objectos-runtime/src/env-settings-door-namespace-coverage.test.ts` lists `knowledge` in `EXPECTED_NAMESPACES` and asserts `builtinSettingsManifests` has length 10; `apps/cloud/test/settings-cross-org-doors.test.ts` lists `knowledge` in `PLATFORM_NAMESPACES` and compares it with the registered set. No hosted behaviour breaks, but the PR body's hosted note does not name them. The cloud lane needs a carrier for the pin move.
- **The earlier record's two should-fixes are unanswered.** Record 6907077911 on #34223 raised the same S1 and S2 as below on `ba9ec457`. This head is that head plus a merge and one pin adjustment; neither is fixed, and the PR body does not mention them.
- **Dev flags and open questions.** The os-dev report carries no open question. The three surface deviations (package entry exports, vitest aliases, the two corpus pins) and the later-added readers (`cloud-managed-settings.pin.test.ts`, the CLI pin) are all counts or imports the change makes false; they belong in the diff. The claim's `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/cloud#4569` correction (7131785382) is supported by the cloud code read in ①.
- **Acceptance 3** is met by the test kernel, as area decision 6898471166 ruled; `examples/app-todo` is unchanged. Acceptance 1 and 2 are read from source (the door's 404 and the console's error card), not driven live.
- **SQL push-down:** the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- **Opened by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`**, with the attribution comment naming `os-warren`; the body's first line carries the seat stamp. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing does what the maintainer ruled: it takes away pages that configured a service no stock deployment mounts, and no consumer in this repository or in the hosted runtime loses a working capability. The mechanism follows the branding precedent already in the tree. Sentence by sentence the code agrees with the contract, with one exception (S1).

S1 (should-fix) — `contributeKnowledgeSettings` recognises "the bundled `ai` page" by key set alone, so the sentence "a host that registered its own `ai` manifest keeps it untouched" is false for one class of host manifest. `knowledge-settings-contribution.ts` lines 106–111: when the registered `ai` manifest has exactly the bundled keys, the function registers `withAiEmbedderSection(aiSettingsManifest)` — the bundled declaration, not the registered one. A host that passed `{ ...aiSettingsManifest, scope, writePermission }` or changed a default or an option table (the pattern cloud's `controlPlaneSettingsManifests` already applies to three other builtins) has its declaration silently replaced, permissions and scope included, with no warning. Tightest fix read in the tree: `servedManifest` returns the registered object itself when the namespace has no option source, so identity with `aiSettingsManifest` is available; or append to the registered declaration; or narrow the claim in the comment, the PR body and the changeset. Either way, pin the two branches that have no test: host manifest (untouched, warning logged) and already-declares-embedder (not re-registered, handler registered). Not a must-fix: no composition in this repository or in cloud mounts the service with a re-declared `ai` page today, and the replacement restores the bundled gate (`manage_platform_settings`, global).

S2 (should-fix) — the changeset says stored `knowledge.*` and `ai.embedder_*` values "stay in the database" and stops. Three of those keys are credentials (`ai.embedder_api_key`, `knowledge.turso_auth_token`, `knowledge.ragflow_api_key`), held as `sys_secret` ciphertext. On a default deployment after this change no served door removes them: `PUT` refuses the key or the namespace, and the built-in `reset` clears declared keys only (`resetNamespaceRows` walks the namespace payload). They also leave the settings attribution set, so `sys-secret-orphan-report.ts` will list them as orphaned. The "What to do" paragraph should tell an operator who wants a stored credential gone how to remove it (mount the service and clear it, or the supported cleanup path), and say that the orphan report will name these rows.

N1 (nit) — the page and its Setup entry are still titled "AI & Embedder" (「AI 与向量化」) in every locale on a deployment that now shows no embedder section. The card names the page by that title and asks only for the section and the description, so this is residue for a follow-up card to decide.

N2 (nit) — "knowledge mounted with no settings service offers nothing and does not throw" is read in the code and has no test.

N3 (nit) — the bundled `ai` description no longer says that `@objectstack/embedder-openai` must be installed on the host, and the embedder group's own description does not say it either, so a deployment that mounts the service loses that hint.

N4 (nit) — a host that passes its own `actionHandlers` with a `knowledge` entry while keeping the default manifests now fails at boot (`registerAction` refuses an unregistered namespace). The changeset says the default map changed; one sentence for this case would help.

Should-fix: S1, S2. Nits: N1–N4. No must-fix.

Delta review, read at 2026-11-24T13:09Z. It follows the record on `8ac823aa649589a8f5c19072864fa3d9c6869823` (PR comment 7132371555) and judges `git diff 8ac823aa..c654ad07`: one commit, three files (the changeset, `knowledge-settings-contribution.ts`, a new test file). Everything outside that delta stands as judged in the earlier record. Same isolated sub-agent, same inputs: the diff, the tree at the head, the PR body and the check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set: unchanged on every composition that exists.** The stock boot and the knowledge-mounted boot over the bundled `ai` page behave as before: `isBundledAiManifest` returns true on identity, which is what `getManifest('ai')` returns when no option source serves an `ai` key (`servedManifest`), and no code in this repository or in cloud registers one (the only registrar is `localization.locale`).
- **Accept-set, host `ai` page with the bundled keys: narrowed back to what the contract says.** A spread copy that changes a manifest field (scope, permission, label), a specifier field other than `options`, the specifier count or the specifier order is no longer taken for the bundled page; it is left as registered and the warning is logged. Right.
- **Public surface:** `isBundledAiManifest` is exported from the module but not from the package entry (`service-knowledge/src/index.ts` is untouched), so nothing new is published. Right.
- **New test file:** seven cases on a real `SettingsService`. The host-page cases assert identity of the registered manifest after the call (`toBe(host)`), absence of every embedder key, and exactly one warning; the already-declares case asserts identity and judges the handler by its own answer; the no-settings case asserts the all-false result. Not vacuous.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch` on the same three packages, the ADR-0087 marker. The delta adds prose to the changeset and no new published symbol.
- The changeset's new "Stored credentials" paragraph is accurate against the tree: the three keys are the encrypted ones, `reset` clears declared keys only, global-scope rows live in `sys_platform_setting`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Check-runs on this head, read at 13:09Z: 37 runs so far — 9 success, 9 skipped, 19 in progress, 0 failure.** `PR-body guards` now reads success, so the stale duplicate-claim red is gone. `Check Changeset`, every test shard and most lint and type-check families were still running. This PASS is not a reading that CI is green; the seat reads convergence.
- **Still escalated: the dogfood battery on the final head.** Unchanged by this commit. The three dogfood shards read `skipped` on this head too (the job excludes `pull_request` events), the bare `Dogfood Regression Gate` reads success over legs that did not run, and the PR body still says the battery runs on the PR's checks and still carries only the `1b210ee4f6` reading. The seat owes the run, or a ruling that the queue run stands in, and a corrected sentence.
- **Still escalated: the two cloud tests** that pin `knowledge` in the default registry (`env-settings-door-namespace-coverage.test.ts`, `settings-cross-org-doors.test.ts`) need a cloud carrier for the pin move. Nothing in this delta bears on it.
- No dev flag or open question arrived with the delta. SQL push-down: the delta adds no query.

### ④ Design judgment

S1: closed. The key-set recognition is gone. `isBundledAiManifest` judges by identity, and the cases the earlier record named (a different scope, a different permission, a different default) are left untouched with a warning, each pinned; the already-declares-embedder branch is pinned too. One slice of the same sentence is still false and is graded on its own as S3.
